subject: Post-call recap + schedule: dedicated sizing for peak traffic (FinBridge)

Subject: Post-call recap + schedule: dedicated sizing for peak traffic (FinBridge)

Hi Liam — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next step so we can lock sizing for the production cutover: 

What we heard (summary)
- Primary goal: move text-generation features into a dedicated pool for predictable latency during peak hours (product search ranking and realtime chat).
- Traffic profile: expected peak concurrency across features, see notes below — you mentioned a heavy burst pattern keyed to marketing pushes.
- Latency target: p95 under 200ms for short prompts (~<300 tokens); agree we should validate with representative prompts.
- Data & compliance: FinBridge needs logs retained 90 days and regional hosting in US.

Proposed next step
- 60-minute dedicated sizing session (throughput + latency deep-dive) with your infra lead + our SEs. We'll run through a sample load profile and settle on pool sizing and fallback policies.
- Proposed windows (please confirm which works for you):
  * Tue Aug 1, 09:00 - 10:00 ET
  * Wed Aug 2, 14:00 - 15:00 ET

Pre-call asks (to speed the session)
- A short CSV with typical payload sizes and expected concurrency (see attached throughput-template.csv)
- A couple of representative prompts (short/long) so we can validate latency expectations

Attachments: post-call-ops-checklist.pdf (high-level agenda & stakeholder list), throughput-template.csv (payload sample)
Call recording: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-recording/finbridge-20280725

If we can lock a slot this week we'll share a calendar invite + runbook ahead of time. Thanks — looking forward.

— Priya

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Liam. Couple of clarifying items so the session is productive: 

1) Workload specifics — please confirm:
  - Average prompt length (tokens) for short vs long flows
  - Typical concurrency vs expected peak bursts (requests/sec)
2) Do you plan to route all production traffic to the dedicated pool at cutover, or will you use a gradual rollout (canary)?
3) Any constraints on GPU types (we can size for A100/RTX or our quantized M2 variants) and maximum permissible prewarming time during cutover window.

I'll also bring a short checklist for KV cache and prefix caching strategies. Attached a fresh copy of throughput-template.csv to populate; if you can return that before Monday we can model expected token throughput and propose an initial pool (GPU + replicas).

Attachments: throughput-template.csv

— Marcus

Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.com>

Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@finbridge.com>
Date: 2028-07-26T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + schedule: dedicated sizing for peak traffic (FinBridge)

Marcus — responding inline to your clarifying questions:

1) Prompt sizes: average short prompt ~180 tokens (search+context), long flows ~1200 tokens (batch repr.), typical payload compressed ~= 4KB.
2) Rollout plan: phased canary — 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two windows. We want the dedicated pool to handle sudden 3x burst from campaigns (planning for safety headroom).
3) We prefer A100 if that's possible; prewarm budget is ~10 minutes during cutover window.

Peak estimates: expect ~350 requests/sec during peak bursts, with sustained ~80-120 rps baseline.

We'll also aim to have Daniel (CTO) on the call; Sara is our infra lead and will own the post-call action items. I'll upload the populated CSV by EOD. Looking forward to the runbook and invite.

— Liam
